quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: If you are 21 or older and have a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher, you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to maintain your balance.
Maintain your speed to improve traction.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when possible. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as you can.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect BAC?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, you should keep what distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: You do not need to worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds between themselves and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when road conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from lane sharing with you?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: From bottom to top, what is the order of traffic light colors?
questions.explanation: From bottom to top, traffic light colors are green, yellow, and red.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is typically used for what?
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show traffic rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
The driver will definitely properly yield to you.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still do not see them.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can do so safely.
Weave within your lane to make yourself more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room for the entering driver.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most crashes happen when the rider has had less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Take extra care when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen with riders who have had less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: You can avoid serious injury by wearing all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while you are braking, release the front brake completely and right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: In a crash, you can avoid serious injury by doing all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Reduce your risk of injury by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Can take corners at any speed.
Should not be used to carry items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for a long time could cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for a long time can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal on a motorcycle is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: After you enter a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly while turning.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Slam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and slam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Use both brakes together when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as fast as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If one tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle while riding straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: You should leave extra space between you and other vehicles:

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally enough. Leave more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as when roads are icy or wet.
